name: Receiver
keywords: radio valve walnut podcast vintage tuning dial brass
idea: A walnut valve radio in a dark room. Content items are stations on the dial; between them the signal breaks into static, and the magic eye closes as you lock on.
note: Live: drag across the dial (it's a native range input underneath, so keyboard arrows work). Watch the station name break up and the green eye open between stations.
borrowed: 1950s tabletop valve radios: arched walnut cabinets, woven speaker cloth with brass threads, backlit cream dial glass, a red needle, piano-key preset buttons, the green "magic eye" tuning tube, and the studio ON AIR sign.
mood: Warm, intimate, after-hours. Suits storytellers, podcasts, writers, music, and personal brands that want warmth instead of tech gloss.

type.meta: Dial & labels · Barlow Condensed 600–700, tabular numerals

motion: Clarity = (1 − distance to nearest station / 1.1)²; drives text garble, static opacity, dial glow and the eye.
Warm-up sweep on load: the needle runs the band and settles on station 1 (2.6s cubic-out).
Static: tiny canvas of noise scaled up with `image-rendering: pixelated`.
Optional audio: band-passed hiss crossfades into a tremolo chord.
watchouts: The dial must stay a real slider (role or native range) with a spoken value that includes the station name.
Garbled text flickers. Stop the flicker under reduced motion.
Brass on walnut is low contrast. Keep it for big display text only.
